'''Arun Mallojirao Jayannavar''' (22 July 1956 - 22 November 2021) was an Indian [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]] and a senior professor at the [[Institute of Physics, Bhubaneswar]]. Known{{whom|date=January 2023}} for his research on many interdisciplinary areas of condensed matter physics, Jayannavar was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies viz. [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and [[Indian National Science Academy]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the government of India for scientific research, awarded Jayannavar the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to physical sciences in 1998.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:Karnataka-University-Dharwad.jpg|thumb|left|Karnataka University, Dharwad]]
Born on 22 July 1956, Arun M. Jayannavar obtained a BSc from Govindram Seksaria Science College, [[Belgaum]], [[Karnataka]] in 1976 and did his master's degree at [[Karnatak University|Karnataka University]] to earn an MSc in 1978.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P02-1316 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-date=17 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017201924/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P02-1316 }}</ref> His doctoral studies were at the [[Indian Institute of Science]] where he was mentored by [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|S. S. Bhatnagar laureates]], [[Narendra Kumar (physicist)]] and [[E. S. Raja Gopal]] and after securing a PhD in 1982, he moved to Italy to do his post-doctoral work at the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) as a visiting scientist. Jayannavar also had a second stint abroad at the [[University of Ulm]] during 1988–90 as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow]]. On his return to India in 1991, he joined the [[Institute of Physics, Bhubaneswar]] as a member of faculty where he holds the position of a senior professor.<ref name="Member of Institute of Physics">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iopb.res.in/members/jayan |title=Member of Institute of Physics |date=2017-10-17 |website=Institute of Physics |access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref> He was also a visiting senior professor at the [[Homi Bhabha National Institute]] of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]], situated in [[Mumbai]].<ref name="HBNI profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.hbni.ac.in/faculty/IOP/iop_phys_arun.htm |title=HBNI profile |date=2017-10-17 |website=Homi Bhabha National Institute |access-date=2017-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018012454/http://www.hbni.ac.in/faculty/IOP/iop_phys_arun.htm |archive-date=18 October 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
[[File:WF111-Anderson transition-multifractal.jpeg|thumb|150px|Anderson transition-multifractal]]
Jayannavar's research interests have been in the interdisciplinary areas of condensed matter physics, with special focus on theoretical condensed matter physics, [[Stochastic processes]], non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, and classical and quantum problems in random media and physics of mesoscopic systems.<ref name="HBNI profile" /><ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=17 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> High temperature superconductors, thermal ratchets and molecular motors, heat pumps at [[nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]]s, [[Anderson localization]], delay times, random lasers, giant diffusion; fluctuation theorems are some of the areas he has worked on and he is reported to have made significant contributions in the elucidation of a number theoretical problems.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=485 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=2017-08-23}}</ref> Jayannavar's studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Arun_Jayannavar |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and the online article repository of the Indian Academy of Sciences has listed 168 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Jayannavar=3AArun_Mallojirao_=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He was also a member of the editorial boards of science journals viz. [[Current Science]] and [[Pramana (journal)|Pramana]]<ref name="Indian fellow" /> and sat in the executive council of Indian Physics Association from 2010 to 2012.<ref name="Executive Committees of IPA">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipa1970.org.in/pastexlist.php |title=Executive Committees of IPA |date=2017-10-17 |website=Indian Physics Association |access-date=2017-10-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170411060234/http://www.ipa1970.org.in/pastexlist.php |archive-date=11 April 2017 }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] awarded Jayannavar the ICTP Prize in the field of solid state physics (in honour of [[Nevill Francis Mott]]) in 1996<ref name="ICTP Prize Winner 1996">{{Cite web |url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-ictp-prize/the-prize-winners/ictp-prize-winner-1996.aspx |title=ICTP Prize Winner 1996 |date=2017-10-17 |website=International Centre for Theoretical Physics |access-date=2017-10-17}}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] elected him as a fellow the same year.<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Jayannavar,_Prof._Arun_Mallojirao |title=Fellow profile |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=2017-10-16}}</ref> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1998.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Gopal |first1=B. Madhu |title="No research possible without the help of nanotechnology" |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/Madurai/%E2%80%9CNo-research-possible-without-the-help-of-nanotechnology%E2%80%9D/article17279518.ece |access-date=1 April 2022 |work=The Hindu |date=10 February 2017 |language=en-IN}}</ref> Two of the other major Indian science academies, [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 }}</ref> and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected Jayannavar as their fellow in 2002 and 2003 respectively<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=J |title=NASI fellows |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-date=7 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707200112/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=J }}</ref> and he received the [[G. D. Birla Award for Scientific Research]] in 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=INSA :: Indian Fellow Detail |url=https://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=P02-1316 |website=www.insaindia.res.in |publisher=insaindia |access-date=1 April 2022}}</ref>
